To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) social networks are an important factor in influencing food choice; 2) the impact of price and norm based messages on meat consumption is influenced by social networks; 3) the impact of social networks on meat consumption depends on how often the norm based messages are given; and 4) the unintended consequences of interventions that target specific groups of people based on their concerns need to be considered.

1) social network influences can be important in changing food choices; 2) the impact of price increases on reducing meat consumption is greater than that of norm-based messages; 3) repeating norm-based messages in the workplace has a greater impact on reducing meat consumption than a one-off intervention; 4) targeting those with greatest concerns about the impact of eating meat on the environment and animal welfare could increase meat consumption in the long term.
social influence can play an important role in shifting the population towards healthier diets.
